title: Largest Ebola Treatment Center in DRC Opens at Kigonze Displacement Camp Near Bunia
detail: International Medical Corps, with UN partnership and US support, opened a 100-bed transit and treatment center at the Kigonze displacement camp on the outskirts of Bunia, Ituri Province — the country's largest single Ebola facility, part of an overall response capacity of roughly 900 beds across five affected provinces. The center will speed identification of suspected cases and referral of confirmed patients, aiming to contain spread within the displacement site. It opened as DRC recorded 567 new cases and 296 deaths in the most recent epidemiological week alone, with active transmission ongoing in 33 of 49 affected health zones. WFP's acting chief said: 'Ebola is moving fast, hitting people already facing conflict and hunger. Communities are key to ending it, but need support.' Separately, the US State Department announced an additional $242 million in Ebola response and preparedness funding for DRC and Uganda on 5 August, bringing total US direct assistance to over $512 million, part of a June G7 commitment of up to $500 million.

title: DRC Ebola Deaths Surpass 1,800 as Health Workers Protest Unpaid Wages
detail: The DRC Ministry of Health reported 3,973 confirmed cases and 1,801 deaths as of 6 August 2026, with roughly 90% of cases concentrated in Ituri Province. Health workers in Bunia protested for a second time, saying they had not received wages or bonuses since the outbreak was declared in mid-May; officials attributed the delays to logistical problems. Protester Edouige Makosi said: 'With this way of managing things, Ebola will not end in this province. We ask the authorities to get involved at all levels so that a solution is found quickly.'
